shared_expansions.P: P f means (for every x in E, f(x) is not bottom) AND (there exist x in E and r in R with f(x)=the finite EReal embedding of r). The finite witness is global and need not lie in V.
shared_expansions.S: g belongs to S f x exactly when, for every y in E, f(x) + embed(<g,y-x>_R) <= f(y) in EReal. Nonemptiness at x means that such a vector g exists. The test variable y ranges over all E, not only V.
shared_expansions.D: D(psi,a,b)=psi(a)-psi(b)-fderiv_R(psi,b)(a-b). The second argument b is the derivative base. D is real valued and ordered; no symmetry, nonnegativity, or metric property follows from its definition.
shared_expansions.IsMinOn: IsMinOn F V p means for every z in V, F(p)<=F(z). Membership p in V is separate. Thus this predicate alone does not assert p in V or existence of an attained minimum within V.
shared_expansions.total_functions: EReal.toReal sends a finite embedded real r to r and sends both top and bottom to 0. It is not a faithful order conversion at infinities. fderiv is a total operation, taking the zero continuous linear map when there is no Frechet derivative. Real inversion is total, with 0 inverse equal to 0.
shared_expansions.finiteness_inference: P f plus S f x nonempty forces f(x) finite: bottom is excluded by P; top is incompatible with the support inequality evaluated at the global finite witness. Consequently the hypotheses of claims 0 and 2 force finiteness on V, without forcing global finiteness.

claims.objects_spaces: E is any real inner product space with NormedAddCommGroup and InnerProductSpace R instances. Completeness is not assumed. f:E->EReal and V is a subset of E.
claims.quantifiers: Universally quantify E and its instances, f, V, and all hypotheses. The support premise is: for every x in V there exists g in E such that for every y in E, f(x)+embed(<g,y-x>)<=f(y).
assumptions: For every y in E, f(y)!=bottom.
There exist y in E and r in R with f(y)=embed(r).
For every x in V there exists g in E with the global support inequality stated in quantifiers.
claims.conclusion: q(x)=toReal(f(x)) is convex on V: V is convex and, for x,y in V and real a,b>=0 with a+b=1, q(a*x+b*y)<=a*q(x)+b*q(y).
claims.constants_normalization: Ordinary real convexity, with nonnegative weights summing to one. The support pairing is the real inner product with coefficient one.
claims.probability_feedback: Deterministic statement. No probability space, random sampling, feedback model, filtration, or oracle complexity is present.
boundary: P and nonempty supports imply finite f on V, which makes toReal faithful there.
Top values outside V are permitted and become zero under toReal. No global convexity is asserted.
V may be empty, and the finite witness in P need not be in V.
No continuity, differentiability, completeness, strict convexity, or minimizer guarantee is assumed or concluded.

claims.quantifiers: Universally quantify all these data. For each data choice satisfying p in V and finiteness of f at every point of V, assert the equivalence below.
assumptions: CompleteSpace E is an explicit typeclass assumption.
For every z in V, f(z)!=top AND f(z)!=bottom.
claims.conclusion: The following predicates are equivalent: (for every z in V, f(p)+embed(eta^(-1)*[psi(p)-psi(x)-fderiv_R(psi,x)(p-x)]) <= f(z)+embed(eta^(-1)*[psi(z)-psi(x)-fderiv_R(psi,x)(z-x)])) and (for every z in V, toReal(f(p))+eta^(-1)*[psi(p)-psi(x)-fderiv_R(psi,x)(p-x)] <= toReal(f(z))+eta^(-1)*[psi(z)-psi(x)-fderiv_R(psi,x)(z-x)]). The first comparison is in EReal and the second in R.
claims.constants_normalization: The regularizer coefficient is eta inverse, not eta. eta is an arbitrary real number, including zero and negatives; at zero its inverse is zero. The derivative base in both D terms is x.
claims.probability_feedback: Deterministic equivalence, with no stochastic or feedback assumptions.
boundary: No convexity of V, f, or psi is assumed.
No positivity or nonzero condition on eta and no differentiability of psi is assumed.
fderiv makes D well-defined even at nondifferentiability; this does not certify an actual derivative there.
x need not belong to V. p membership is explicit and separate from IsMinOn, ensuring finiteness at p.
This equates minimizer predicates for a supplied p; it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness nor a numeric minimum.
Completeness is part of the written interface even if the order-conversion interpretation does not visibly need it.
